What is the exact enrollment or policy sync error shown?
Is this affecting one device or a group of devices in a policy scope?
What was the last successful check-in time for this device?
Has the device ever successfully checked in with Intune/MDM before, or has it never enrolled successfully at all?
Is this a new enrollment issue, a policy application issue, or an ongoing compliance/reporting issue?

l1: Check Settings > Accounts > Access work or school for enrollment status.
Run 'dsregcmd /status' to confirm Azure AD join and MDM URL state.
Force a sync via Settings > Accounts > Info > Sync.
Check the Intune portal for the device's last check-in timestamp.
l2: Run 'mdmdiagnosticstool.exe /area DeviceEnrollment /cab C:\diag.cab' for full logs.
Review Event Viewer > Applications and Services > Microsoft > Windows > DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider.
Check Intune policy assignment reports for conflict or error status.
Review co-management workload configuration in the SCCM console.

l1: Force a manual sync from Settings > Access work or school.
Restart the device and confirm sync resumes after reboot.
Confirm the device has network connectivity to Intune endpoints.
Re-check the group membership targeting this device for the policy.
Confirm the device shows up at all in the Intune portal before troubleshooting policy application — an invisible device is an enrollment problem, not a policy problem.
For Autopilot specifically, confirm the device's hardware hash was actually uploaded and matched to the correct Autopilot profile before assuming a general enrollment fault.
l2: Unenroll and re-enroll the device if MDM certificate is invalid or expired.
Resolve conflicting GPO settings that override the intended Intune policy.
Repair the MDM enrollment certificate via 'certutil' if expired.
Adjust the co-management workload slider to hand off the conflicting workload.

Confirm the Azure AD join type and dsregcmd output.
Note which specific policy or app is failing to apply.

Collect the Intune policy assignment and deployment status report.

policy_not_applying.title: Intune policy assigned but not applying to device

steps.action: Confirm the device is in the correct assignment group in Intune
steps.expect: Device appears as a member of the targeted group

steps.action: Check the per-device policy status in the Intune portal
steps.expect: Status shows Error, Conflict, or Pending with a reason

steps.action: Resolve the identified conflict, such as a competing GPO

steps.expect: Device check-in updates with new policy status

steps.action: Verify the setting is applied locally on the device
steps.expect: Local setting matches the intended Intune configuration

device_shows_noncompliant_unexpectedly.title: Device shows as Not Compliant in Intune despite meeting requirements

steps.action: Check the device's Compliance status blade in Intune for which specific policy/setting is failing
steps.expect: Identifies the exact non-compliant setting rather than assuming a general enrollment problem

steps.action: Compare the device's actual local setting against what the compliance policy expects, and check the device's last compliance evaluation timestamp
steps.expect: Confirms whether the device is stale (hasn't reported recently) or genuinely out of compliance

steps.action: Force a sync from Settings > Access work or school, or remediate the specific out-of-compliance setting directly
steps.expect: Device re-evaluates and reports current, accurate state

steps.action: Re-check the Compliance status blade after the next check-in

autopilot_enrollment_fails_at_oobe.title: Autopilot enrollment fails or hangs during OOBE

steps.action: Confirm the device's hardware hash is registered under the correct Autopilot deployment profile in Intune
steps.expect: Confirms the device is recognized and correctly profiled

steps.action: Check network connectivity to required Autopilot/Intune endpoints during OOBE, and review the specific OOBE error code/screen shown
steps.expect: Identifies whether it's a network reachability issue or a profile/policy assignment issue

steps.action: Resolve the identified blocker — fix network access, correct the Autopilot profile assignment, or re-register the hardware hash if mismatched
Reset the device and retry OOBE end-to-end
steps.expect: Device completes Autopilot enrollment and applies its assigned profile

co_management_workload_conflict.title: Co-managed device applies conflicting settings from SCCM and Intune

steps.action: Confirm the device is genuinely co-managed and identify the specific setting behaving inconsistently
steps.expect: Confirms co-management status and isolates the conflicting setting

steps.action: Check the co-management workload slider in the SCCM console for the workload area covering that setting (e.g. Device Configuration, Compliance)
steps.expect: Identifies which authority (SCCM or Intune) is currently supposed to own that workload

steps.action: Move the workload slider fully to the intended authority (Intune or SCCM/ConfigMgr) rather than leaving it split, and remove the conflicting policy from the other side
steps.expect: Only one authority manages that setting going forward

steps.action: Force a policy refresh and confirm the setting now applies consistently
steps.expect: No further conflicting policy application for that setting
